ACID: atomicity, consistency, isolation, durability, the guarantees of a database transaction
ACK: acknowledgement, a TCP flag confirming received data
ASCII: American standard code for information interchange
AVL: Adelson-Velsky and Landis, the inventors of the self-balancing tree
CD: continuous delivery or continuous deployment, releasing every change that passes the pipeline
CDC: change data capture, reading a database's change log to stream every committed change
CQRS: command query responsibility segregation, separate models for writing and reading
CSV: comma-separated values, a plain-text table format
DI: dependency injection, handing a class its dependencies instead of letting it create them
DIP: dependency inversion principle, the D in SOLID
DRY: don't repeat yourself, keep each piece of knowledge in one place
DTO: data transfer object, a plain shape for data crossing a boundary such as a request body
DWARF: the debugging data format that accompanies ELF binaries
E2E: end to end, a test that drives the whole running application the way a user does
FIN: finish, the TCP flag that begins a connection teardown
INI: initialisation file, a simple key=value configuration format
KISS: keep it simple, stupid, prefer the simplest solution that meets the requirement
LSP: Liskov substitution principle, the L in SOLID
OCP: open/closed principle, the O in SOLID
PPM: portable pixmap, a plain-text image format
RFC: request for comments, the document series that specifies internet protocols
RST: reset, the TCP flag that aborts a connection
SHA: secure hash algorithm; in Git, the hash identifying a commit
SMS: short message service, a text message
SOLID: single responsibility, open/closed, Liskov substitution, interface segregation, dependency inversion
SPFA: shortest path faster algorithm, a queue-based refinement of Bellman-Ford
SQS: Simple Queue Service, Amazon's managed message queue
SRP: single responsibility principle, the S in SOLID
SWE: software engineering, or a software engineer
SYN: synchronise, the TCP flag that opens a connection
TAP: a virtual network interface carrying Ethernet frames
TDD: test-driven development, writing a failing test before the code
TUN: a virtual network interface carrying IP packets
USSD: unstructured supplementary service data, menus reached by dialling a short code on a phone
YAGNI: you aren't gonna need it, don't build for a requirement that hasn't arrived
